title: Does High Humidity Raise Your Blood Pressure?
description: Yes — studies show blood pressure can rise up to 10 mmHg in humid heat (≥70% RH + >80°F). Learn how to protect your heart this summer.
reasoning: A summer heatwave is driving real-time searches from adults 35+ worried about sudden BP spikes during humid conditions — they want practical, evidence-based guidance on monitoring, prevention, and when to seek help, not clinical jargon.

title: What’s a Normal Pulse Rate Variation After 35?
primaryKeyword: normal pulse rate variation for adults over 35
description: Resting pulse can safely vary by 20–30 bpm day-to-day—yet sudden jumps >40 bpm may signal stress or early heart strain. Learn what’s normal, what’s not, and when to act.
reasoning: People over 35 are noticing unexplained pulse fluctuations—especially post-pandemic fatigue, rising stress, and increased wearable use—and conflating normal variation with danger; they want clear, age-specific thresholds (not textbook ranges) and actionable red flags, not medical jargon.
